title: host oom gradual leak signal correlation diary
body:
Summary:

This is a working diary capturing the on-call observations, hypotheses, and temporary mitigations for a series of low-velocity host OOMs we observed across a subset of serving-runtime GPU hosts in eu-west-1 between 2024-11-12 and 2024-11-15.

Key distinguishing characteristics: compact, reproducible pattern unlike single huge OOM events - memory usage slowly climbs over multiple hours, evictions start occurring more frequently, host-level OOMs follow (~10-20% of affected hosts), but coredumps aren't present and kernel oom_killer doesn't consistently log. KV-cache growth and prefetch amplification are strongly correlated.

Timeline (high level):
- 2024-11-12 01:23 UTC: first alert - host-34c shows increasing memoryballoon alerts on Grafana. Not an immediate OOM, just queueing/responses slower.
- 2024-11-12 04:10 UTC: tokenshedder spikes on host-34c; evictions increase, request latencies climb.
- 2024-11-12 06:05 UTC: host-34c transiently reports ENOMEM to userland process, service recovers after restart of service process.
- 2024-11-13 22:10 UTC: similar pattern observed on host-11a and host-78b; slower slope of memory increase, multiple small spikes, then fatal OOM on host-78b.
- 2024-11-14 03:14 UTC: SRE escalation. We put a temporary dynconfig limiting prefetch concurrency to 6 for the affected fleet.
- 2024-11-14 08:00 UTC: eviction rate drops by ~45% across the flagged hosts, but host memory slope still non-zero.
- 2024-11-15 01:00 UTC: scheduled maintenance: rotate kernel jemalloc tuning on a small canary (host-11a) and enable compact-on-threshold prototype.

Telemetry correlations we pulled: (notes to self)
- kv_live_entry_count (per-host) increases roughly linearly over time for affected hosts; slope strongly matches host RSS growth.
- prefetch_outstanding_reqs correlates to small bursts in RSS but not sufficient to explain total growth.
- jemalloc fragmentation ratio (sampled via /proc/<pid>/smaps + exported metric) shows slow drift from 1.05 -> 1.35 over 48 hours on affected processes.
- swap usage reported 0 bytes on these hosts (swap disabled), but cgroup.memory.events shows repeated "oom" events even when kernel didn't kill.
- container memory.high pressure triggers earlier than host OOM; in several cases the cgroup VM reclamation path incorrectly reported success while RSS continued climbing.

Initial hypotheses (ranked):
1) Gradual KV cache retention growth due to a change in prefetch heuristics plus a subtle race that prevents TTL eviction from running under sustained backpressure. This increments live entries and fragments allocator causing RSS drift. (high confidence)
2) A jemalloc regression interacting with contiguous allocator arenas under multi-threaded continuous batching, causing internal fragmentation and delayed free coalescing (medium confidence).
3) Kernel/cgroup bookkeeping mismatch with cgroup v2 memory controllers: under heavy GPU scheduling and perf isolation, memory.high throttling misfires and userland continues to allocate (low/medium confidence).
4) External GC-like activity (not very likely) - e.g., user workloads with monstrous prompt sequences. (low confidence)

Immediate actions taken during on-call:
- Decreased prefetch concurrency fleet-wide for eu-west-1 serving hosts (dynconfig) to throttle new KV growth.
- Bumped eviction aggressiveness in the local runtime config (ttl shortening from 15m -> 3m) for a narrow canary.
- Added ephemeral autoscaling capacity for high-traffic customers to reduce per-host pressure.
- For hosts that hit fatal OOM we performed controlled service restarts and then evacuated tenants off the host.

Observed effects after mitigations:
- Within 4 hours eviction rate decreased and latency partially recovered.
- RAM growth slope reduced but did not flatten on all hosts; a subset still drifted upwards at low slope (~40–60 MB/hour).
- Canary with jemalloc compact-on-threshold showed reduced fragmentation metric and started to stabilize (sample size: 1 host).

Runbook draft (triage checklist) - immediate on-call steps:
1) Identify the topology: list affected host IDs via grafana filter (memory.rss > host baseline + 1.5 stddev for > 30 minutes).
2) Correlate service-level metrics: kv_live_entry_count, prefetch_outstanding_reqs, eviction_rate, tokenshedder_drops.
3) If kv_live_entry_count slope > X (heuristic: > 200 entries/hour), apply temporary prefetch throttling dynconfig to that host pool.
4) If eviction_rate > baseline*3 and latency > 250ms, promote host to maintenance: drain new traffic, restart runtime, collect jemalloc profile.
5) For hosts with fatal OOM: capture dmesg + container logs, snapshot /proc/<pid>/smaps, mark host for deep forensic (do NOT reboot cluster without evacuation).
6) If multiple hosts in same AZ show the pattern, raise INC with infra and networking to check cross-host page reclaim anomalies.

Recommended longer-term engineering tasks (follow-ups):
- INF-842: implement kv_live_entry_count export for every tenant and a rolling slope alarm + grafana dashboard. (owner: Jamal)
- SRE-1129: prototype and A/B jemalloc compact-on-threshold across controlled percentage of fleet. Collect fragmentation ratios, RSS slopes, observed latencies. (owner: Marta)
- PR 3812: add a prefetch-backpressure path that abandons speculative fetches if eviction pressure exceeds threshold to avoid amplification loops. (owner: runtime team)
- Instrument a user-level periodic compactor job that can run opportunistically during low load windows to release fragmented arenas back to OS. (owner: serving-runtime)
- Add cgroup memory controller cross-checks in host agent: compare cgroup.events and /proc/<pid>/status counters to detect misreports and surface to SRE alerts. (owner: infra/agent)

Data collection & forensics checklist (what to capture before restart):
- /proc/<pid>/smaps (or jemalloc stats endpoint) + malloc_stats logs
- cgroup v2 memory.events and memory.stat snapshot
- host dmesg (kernel OOM logs), kube kubelet logs for eviction events
- perf top / pmap of large allocations if possible
- timeline of prefetch and eviction metrics (1h before, 6h before)

Notes / open questions: 
- Why did kernel oom_killer not trigger consistently? There are hints that cgroup reclaim succeeded briefly (memory pressure solved) but userland retained references so RSS continued climbing; need to verify reclaim paths.
- The jemalloc fragmentation metric is our best signal so far but sampled only on a few hosts. We should add an exported metric for fragmentation ratio and arena count.
- Are certain model types or request patterns (batch size, seq length) responsible for uneven growth? Need to join product/solutions data.

Possible mitigation knobs to add to runtime config (design notes):
- adaptive-prefetch: pause speculative fetches when host_eviction_rate > threshold OR kv_live_entry_count_slope > threshold.
- soft-compact-trigger: call mallctl("arenas.purge", ...) asynchronously when fragmentation_ratio > 1.2 and CPU load < 30%.
- tenant-isolation-shedder: move long-lived KV entries to a secondary cold store when live_count > tenant_quota.

Owner & next steps: 
- Short-term owner (SRE): Liam Carter to coordinate canary rollout of compact-on-threshold and observe for 48h.
- Long-term owner (runtime): Marta Silva to spec adaptive-prefetch & eviction-shedding; link infra to schedule implementation.
- Instrumentation owner: Jamal Ortiz to push kv_live_entry_count and fragmentation ratio metrics to prod.

Action items (small checklist):
- [ ] Create INF ticket to add kv_live_entry_count export (Jamal)
- [ ] Add jemalloc fragmentation metric to node_exporter or runtime endpoint (Marta)
- [ ] Ship temporary dynconfig limiting prefetch concurrency to 6 for eu-west-1 (SRE oncall)
- [ ] Draft new runbook entry for gradual-leak pattern and add to serving-runtime oncall playbook (Aisha)

Notes-to-self: keep this doc as a mutable diary. Do not finalize until we have 72h of stable telemetry across canaries. Also, check historical rollouts on 2024-10-20 for prefetch heuristic change (possible rollout cause).

Appendix: quick commands for oncall
- list hosts with rising RSS: curl -s "https://api.metrics/hosts?filter=region:eu-west-1&metric=memory.rss&since=2h" | jq ".[] | select(.slope > 100000) | .host"
- fetch jemalloc stats (if endpoint enabled): curl http://HOST:9101/metrics/jemalloc | grep fragmentation_ratio

End of diary entry (draft).
